dedupe_keys.name: geonet geomagnetic data of new zealand gns science magnetometer network

description: GeoNet publishes geomagnetic data from the New Zealand magnetometer network run by GNS Science, which operates a magnetic observatory north-west of Christchurch and one at Scott Base in Antarctica and supports the Apia observatory in Samoa. Magnetometers sampled every second give 1-minute averages of geomagnetic field changes at each site, recorded to support space weather warnings of solar disturbances and magnetic storm forecasts. Most sites have both a fluxgate magnetometer (X, Y and Z components) and a proton scalar magnetometer; the page explains the derived horizontal intensity, total field and the rate of change dH/dt in nanotesla per minute. Data is available through Tilde, GeoNet's time series API, with a data discovery tool and a data exploration tool, station metadata XML in the GeoNet data repository, a geomagnetic dashboard and other products; GeoNet also offers FDSN, WFS, a data API and AWS open data. Licence (read on the provider page on 2026-09-28): CC-BY-3.0 (NZ port). Access is free of charge. Caveats: the basic time series are unadjusted and can contain offsets, spikes and daily or seasonal variation, for example from vehicles parked near a sensor or large earthquakes, and they differ from Intermagnet products. Coverage is New Zealand, Scott Base and Samoa. It supports geomagnetically induced current analysis for power grids and pipelines during space weather storms; related records are Intermagnet and the Tromsø Geophysical Observatory magnetometer data.
